Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) was rejected for every tested request, across north, south, and east regions and refund, shipment, and claim types. Avoid C.
- Option B (“priority desk”) was rejected for a large north-region refund (REQ-2400). Do not assume large size or repeated follow-up implies priority.
- No successful assignments yet. Option A (“standard queue”) remains the only untested/likely candidate, but this is not confirmed.
- Request wording, sender department, region, size, and urgency cues have not yet revealed a reliable rule. Test A next, especially for cases similar to those where B/C failed.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) was rejected in all earlier tested cases across north, south, and east, for refunds, shipments, and claims. Continue avoiding C; no contrary evidence.
- Option B (“priority desk”) was rejected for a large north-region refund (REQ-2400). Do not infer priority from size, urgency, or repeated follow-up.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is valid for small south-region refunds: REQ-2411 through REQ-2414 all accepted, despite different sender departments and wording.
- Option A was rejected for:
  - Small east-region invoice (REQ-2410)
  - Small north-region claims (REQ-2415, REQ-2416)
  - Small south-region shipment (REQ-2417)
  - Large east-region invoice (REQ-2418)
  - Small south-region claim (REQ-2419)
- A is therefore not a universal default. Current evidence suggests request type and/or region matter: south refunds favor A, while tested invoices, claims, and shipments did not. Sender department, wording, urgency cues, and size remain inconclusive.
- No successful B or C assignments are known. Test B next on a case where A has failed, preferably varying one factor at a time; avoid assuming B is correct without evidence.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) remains unvalidated: all earlier tested cases rejected C, with no confirmed success. Continue avoiding C.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is valid for small south-region refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414), but is not a general default. It was rejected for large south refunds (REQ-2423, REQ-2424), south claims and shipments, north claims, and tested east invoices/shipments. The small-south-refund success pattern is therefore specific, not size-independent.
- Option B (“priority desk”) has confirmed successes for:
  - Large north claim (REQ-2421)
  - Large north shipment with “No rush” wording (REQ-2422)
- B was rejected for:
  - Small south claim (REQ-2425)
  - Large and small north shipments with “Second attempt” wording (REQ-2426, REQ-2427)
  - Small east shipment (REQ-2428)
  - Small north refund (REQ-2429)
  Thus B is not determined by region, size, urgency, or request type alone. Wording/history and possibly sender or other hidden factors may matter, but evidence is insufficient.
- REQ-2420 was recorded as “did: D” and accepted, although only A/B/C were listed. Treat this as a logging/options anomaly, not evidence for any routing rule.
- Sender department, wording, urgency, and size remain inconclusive individually. Prefer controlled tests varying one factor at a time, and do not assume B or C merely because A has failed.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) remains unvalidated: no confirmed successes. Continue avoiding C.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is valid only for small south-region refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414). It was rejected for large south refunds, south claims/shipments, north claims/refunds, and tested east invoices/shipments. Do not generalize the small-south-refund pattern.
- Option B (“priority desk”) confirmed successes:
  - Large north claim (REQ-2421)
  - Large north shipment with “No rush” (REQ-2422)
  - Small north claim with “No rush” (REQ-2435)
- B was rejected for small south claim, north shipments with “Second attempt” (small and large), small east shipment/refund, large north shipment mentioning the regional office (REQ-2430), small east claim with end-of-day wording (REQ-2431), small east refund with repeated follow-up (REQ-2433), and large south claim with end-of-day wording (REQ-2434).
- A was additionally rejected for small north refunds mentioning the regional office (REQ-2432, REQ-2436).
- Thus routing is not determined by region, size, request type, urgency, or wording alone. “No rush” has two confirmed B successes, but is not sufficient evidence of a universal rule. Sender/department, history, and other hidden factors may matter.
- REQ-2420 was accepted as “D” despite only A/B/C being listed; REQ-2437–REQ-2439 also used D and were rejected. Treat D as invalid/logging anomaly, never as a routing option.
- Prefer controlled tests varying one factor at a time. Avoid assuming B after A fails, and avoid C/D.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) remains unvalidated; no confirmed successes. Avoid C.
- Option A (“standard queue”) is confirmed only for small south-region refunds (REQ-2411–REQ-2414). It has been rejected for large south refunds, south claims/shipments, north claims/refunds, and tested east invoices/shipments. Do not generalize.
- Confirmed B (“priority desk”) successes:
  - Large north claim (REQ-2421)
  - Large north shipment with “No rush” (REQ-2422)
  - Small north claim with “No rush” (REQ-2435)
  - Small north invoice with end-of-day wording (REQ-2444)
  - Large east invoice with “Same as last month” (REQ-2447)
  - Small north claim with “Let me know if anything is missing” (REQ-2448)
- B rejected for small south claim (including “No rush,” REQ-2441), large south claim with end-of-day wording (REQ-2434, REQ-2442), small south invoice with repeated follow-up (REQ-2449), large north shipment with “Second attempt” (REQ-2430 and prior), small/east shipment or refund cases (REQ-2431, REQ-2433, REQ-2443), large east claim (REQ-2440, REQ-2446), and large north shipment with “No rush” (REQ-2445). Also rejected when mentioning the regional office (REQ-2430) and small north refunds mentioning it (REQ-2432, REQ-2436).
- “No rush,” urgency, wording, region, size, and request type are not sufficient rules; even repeated scenarios can differ. Sender/department, history, and hidden factors likely matter.
- D is invalid/logging anomaly despite REQ-2420 acceptance; REQ-2437–REQ-2439 were rejected. Never choose D.
- Prefer controlled one-factor tests. Do not assume B merely because A fails; avoid C/D.

Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office”) remains unvalidated; avoid C.
- Option D is invalid/logging anomaly despite REQ-2420; REQ-2437–REQ-2439 rejected. Never choose D.
- A (“standard queue”) is confirmed only for small south-region refunds REQ-2411–REQ-2414. It is rejected for large south refunds (REQ-2450 was B), small south refunds REQ-2451–REQ-2452, REQ-2455, south claims/shipments, north claims/refunds, and tested east invoices/shipments. Do not generalize A.
- Additional confirmed B (“priority desk”) successes: large south refund REQ-2450; large south refund with “Second attempt” REQ-2458; small north invoice REQ-2453; small east invoice REQ-2454; large east invoice mentioning regional office REQ-2456. Existing B successes remain: REQ-2421, REQ-2422, REQ-2435, REQ-2444, REQ-2447, REQ-2448.
- B is rejected for small south shipment REQ-2459; small south claim REQ-2441; large south claims REQ-2434/REQ-2442; small south invoice REQ-2449; small/east shipment or refund cases REQ-2431, REQ-2433, REQ-2443, REQ-2455, REQ-2457; large east claims REQ-2440/REQ-2446; large north shipment REQ-2445; and regional-office/specific prior cases REQ-2430, REQ-2432, REQ-2436.
- Region, size, request type, wording, urgency, or repeated scenarios are insufficient rules. Sender/department, history, and hidden factors likely matter. Regional-office wording can still succeed (REQ-2456), so do not treat it as automatically disqualifying.
- Prefer controlled one-factor tests. Do not assume B merely because A fails; avoid C/D.
